findings.title: Retry-count delete clause deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate<=now}, {retryCount:{gt:1}}]. The second branch has no method: SMS filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 is deleted regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and regardless of scheduled/scheduledDate. The comment and intent is SMS-only cleanup. This causes data loss for other channels if they ever use retryCount and can delete future scheduled reminders. Fix by AND-ing method SMS (and scheduled:false) into the retryCount branch.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
findings.body: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts both failure paths do data: {retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1} using the value read at the start of the cron run. If two cron invocations overlap or the same reminder is processed concurrently, both read the same value and write back the same increment, losing one retry. The reminder can then never reach the >1 threshold and be retried forever. Use atomic Prisma update data: {retryCount: {increment: 1}} instead of read-modify-write.

findings.title: Missing number / empty message never counts as retry
findings.body: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the send is guarded by if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) with no else. When sendTo is missing/empty (e.g. invalid or absent smsReminderNumber, the exact case this PR claims to fix) or message is empty, the loop does nothing: no scheduled flag, no retryCount increment. The same row is fetched again on every cron tick until scheduledDate passes, defeating the 2-strike retry limit. The same applies to the continue when workflowStep/booking is missing. Increment retryCount or delete in those no-op paths.
